description: We're planning to solve real-world problems by combining space technology and fishing!
summary:
FishShift is an interactive web application that connects space technology with sustainable fishing.

Fishing communities face growing challenges as ocean temperatures, marine ecosystems, and environmental conditions change. Traditional fishing decisions often rely on experience, making it difficult to understand long-term environmental trends and identify suitable fishing areas efficiently.

FishShift addresses these challenges by combining NASA satellite observations with marine biodiversity data. Users can select fish species, explore sea surface temperature and chlorophyll-a distributions, and visualize how ocean conditions have changed over time. The platform also provides statistical trend analysis and an experimental route comparison tool that estimates fuel consumption under different simulated marine conditions.

Our goal is to transform complex Earth observation data into accessible, practical information that supports smarter fishing decisions.

By connecting ocean science with everyday challenges, FishShift demonstrates how space technology can help reduce unnecessary exploration, improve environmental awareness, and contribute to a more sustainable future for fisheries and marine ecosystems.
details:
1. Key Features

FishShift provides three main capabilities designed to connect Earth observation science with practical fishing decisions.

Ocean Environment and Fish Habitat Explorer

Users can select fish species, including Pacific bluefin tuna, chum salmon, and Japanese sardines, and explore different ocean regions.

The interactive map displays NASA-derived sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll-a concentration, alongside historical fish occurrence records from the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS).

Users can switch between environmental layers, select observation periods, and examine potential habitat suitability. These indicators help users explore environmental conditions relevant to different species.

Ocean Trend Analysis

FishShift analyzes historical NASA observations to reveal long-term changes in ocean conditions.

The application presents time-series charts, estimated rates of change, statistical significance, and confidence intervals.

This functionality directly addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge, "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!", by helping users understand what is changing, where changes occur, and whether the detected trends are statistically significant.

Fuel-Aware Route Comparison

FishShift includes an experimental route-planning simulator.

Users can compare alternative routes to selected fishing-area candidates and adjust vessel speed, fuel consumption, and fuel prices.

The simulator evaluates travel distance, estimated fuel consumption, and costs using simplified marine-condition assumptions.

The results demonstrate how environmental information could support more fuel-efficient decisions. They are illustrative estimates, not validated fuel savings or operational navigation guidance.

2. How It Works

FishShift combines multiple sources of environmental and biodiversity information.

NASA satellite-derived datasets provide historical sea surface temperature and chlorophyll-a observations. OBIS provides historical species occurrence records.

The application processes these datasets into geographic grids and time-series information. Users can interactively explore different regions, species, environmental variables, and observation periods.

For trend detection, FishShift applies statistical analysis to historical observations to estimate long-term changes and evaluate their significance.

For route comparison, a simplified mathematical model estimates travel time, fuel consumption, and cost using user-defined vessel parameters and simulated environmental conditions.

The current prototype distinguishes observed data from estimated or simulated information.

3. Benefits and Expected Impact

FishShift aims to provide three major benefits.

Environmental: Make ocean changes more accessible and improve awareness of marine ecosystem conditions.

Economic: Support more efficient fishing-area exploration and investigate opportunities to reduce unnecessary fuel consumption.

Scientific and Educational: Help users understand satellite observations, historical environmental trends, and the importance of statistical evidence.

By making complex Earth science data easier to explore, FishShift creates a connection between scientific research and real-world decision-making.

4. Development Technologies

The project was developed as an interactive web application using:

  • Programming languages: TypeScript and JavaScript
  • Frontend: React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS
  • Data visualization: Interactive maps, charts, and custom SVG components
  • Scientific computation: JavaScript-based statistical calculations
  • Data sources: NASA Earth observation datasets and OBIS marine biodiversity records
  • Development and version control: Git and GitHub
  • Hosting and deployment: Vercel
  • Development assistance: AI-assisted planning and code generation

The application runs in a standard web browser and does not require specialized hardware or user registration.

5. Future Goals

Our long-term vision is to create a science-based decision-support platform for sustainable fisheries.

Future development will focus on integrating more marine observations, improving species-specific habitat models, incorporating validated weather and ocean forecasts, and evaluating route optimization using real vessel performance and fishing data.

We also aim to expand geographical coverage and make ocean intelligence accessible to fishing communities around the world.

FishShift represents a first step toward transforming space-based environmental observations into practical, responsible, and sustainable fishing decisions.
